description: Residential fence panel of a low rendered masonry wall topped by vertical square steel pickets with spear finials between brick piers, painted dark green.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Residential fence panel with a low rendered masonry wall at the base, a rendered square pier at each end with a pyramid cap, and a panel of vertical square steel pickets with spear-point finials and two horizontal rails between the piers, pickets painted dark green Materials: Cream render stained with rain streaks and black mildew at the base, dark green enamel on the pickets chipped to rust at the rails, a cracked pier cap.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 852/4,000 triangles, 4/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 4/6 unique geometries, three canvases at 3.0 MB, factory ~60 ms. Turntable: the picket bay is open by nature, allowed on measurement; 90/270 are UNSEGMENTABLE by size (pier under the segmenter's 3.5% floor), recorded as a gate limitation of every 3 m panel.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 3.02 x 1.80 x 0.38 m (one pier per tile, wall and rails 0.02 m past the edge); wall 0.60 m, rails 0.70/1.44 m, tips 1.65 m off the proxy's 0.33/0.78/0.92 H; the pier 0.32 m and its cap 0.38 m are the proxy's 9 and 11 columns of 80. Band table: mean |delta width| 0.044, |delta depth| 0.020.
featureReviews.notes: The cap's 0.38 m is the proxy's reading over the declared 0.30 m depth; the residual is the declaration.

featureReviews.evidence: Fourteen instanced 38 mm square-bar pickets (the plate's 28 px of a 120 px pitch at 207 px/m, the proxy's one column) running from the wall top through the lower rail to a collar and a DIAMOND spear that flares to 62 mm and tapers 110 mm to the tip, flat-shaded (4-segment cylinders un-indexed so they facet instead of shading round); 0.06 m flat-bar rails BEHIND the pickets, 14 mm back. Pitch 0.191 m against the proxy's 0.19. Orange rust at the welds and along the rails from a paint canvas over a rust-envelope vertex colour.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's 22 mm pickets and 35 mm square rails were half the plate's bar; its rust multiplied INTO the green and rendered as black spots.

featureReviews.evidence: Cream render at the measured #cfc6b0 on the wall and #cdc4ae on the pier, each on its own material because each carries a different stain: the wall's HARD black mildew as ten colonies of 300 blotches at alpha 0.35-0.85 over a 0.8 ground wash (the plate's colonies at luma 20-45), with black drips hanging off the wall top under the picket feet from the grime tile's joint band at v 0.441; the pier's 34 black rain streaks 1-8 cm wide from the cap edges over a dark base wash.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's mildew was a 0.32 grey wash of soft dots. The cap slab's flat top smears the streak tile into faint stripes under height UVs; the plate's cracked cap is not modelled as a crack.

name: Steel Picket Property Fence
nameTh: รั้วเหล็กดัด
notes: The middle-class house and shophouse fence, and the wall of most Bangkok schools. Piers at both ends so it tiles pier to pier; a matching gate is a separate asset if needed. Placement overridden to floor. Not breakable. One post per tile: the post is on the -X end and the bay runs to the +X edge, so tiles chain along X with no doubled post at a joint.
